Man, I lived in CA for 8 years (SF and San Diego). The fire season is terrifying, I don't know how people deal with the dread of it their whole lives. Even if a fire is far away, it doesn't matter because embers get airborne and can literally drop down anywhere and start another one. I knew several people in Rancho Bernardo who had houses in the morning that were burnt down to the ground by the afternoon. One time, the fires burned up to the top of the I-5 embankment three blocks from my house. That is some capital-S Stress.

Funny thing, I don't feel stress. I live in the south Sierra and there's at least one big fire a year, not counting all the small grass ones or river fires. I've lived here the majority of my life and you just get used to the idea that it could burn up in an evening. But that's true wherever you are, in one sense or another. Clearing fire hazards around houses also helps.

Then again, I don't have a family or any large animals to worry about, I don't live in town, and I can rebuild my own house if I need to.
